correctness.rationale: Equation (1) follows from signed one-pattern overlap clusters. Equation (2) forces equality of unweighted overlap polynomials from counts through length 2m-1; equation (3) forces equality of marked counts in each overlap, hence equality of full bivariate functions. The explicit two-one witness family proves sharpness for every m>=4 and the two-set example proves a strict boundary. Independent computations cover 630 patterns and 932 direct brute-force histograms; finite experiments are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The finite first-jet determination problem is motivated by recent work on letter frequency in one-factor-avoidance shifts. A sharp cutoff reconstructs every higher marked-letter distribution without full weighted enumeration, and a minimal natural change to two forbidden factors invalidates it. This is a structural identifiability theorem with a sharp infinite witness family, not an arbitrary small census.
